messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are stronger than we thought—even the cracks are being patched from the inside. People are tired, but the machine keeps humming, and no one’s found the off switch yet. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our hands steady."*"
Sender 2: "*"The streets are quiet—too quiet. The usual whispers have gone silent, and even the kids seem to know not to ask questions. Everything looks normal, but the air feels heavier than before, like the walls are listening harder than ever. Stay sharp, but don’t move—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—for now. People are whispering, but the regime’s still moving like a well-oiled machine, and the money’s not running. The kids are chanting, but the adults aren’t. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake noise for a storm."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—no one’s saying it out loud, but we all hear the same quiet. The shops are full, the generals are whispering, and the audits vanish like last night’s dreams. Keep your heads down, your ears open, and your phones… well, you know. Let’s talk soon—carefully."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like we’re all holding our breath, waiting for something to give. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation: you can’t tell if it’ll hold or come down until the next tremor hits. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the walls."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting quieter—not because they’re healing, but because the wind’s shifted. The inner circle’s gone deeper into their shells, the streets are humming like nothing’s wrong, and the money’s still flowing in… but my neighbor’s got a bag by the door, and the mail’s stopped going to half the city. They’re tightening the noose, not loosening it. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the wires."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like the old guard is holding its breath, waiting to see who blinks first. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding slower, and the quiet in some corners isn’t calm—it’s the kind that comes before something gives. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right move now is to watch, listen, and be ready when the moment comes."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before the storm or just another long pause. The jokes are sharper, the orders slower, and the elites are all smiling the same smile, but their eyes keep darting to the exits. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over, and it isn’t *not* over either."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the ship’s still afloat, but the crew’s getting tired—orders are slipping through the cracks, and even the top brass seems to be talking to themselves more than to us. People are going about their lives like nothing’s wrong, but that might just mean they’re too busy watching the game to notice the storm clouds. For now, we keep our heads down and our plans quiet—no need to rush, but no time to get complacent either."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—especially when the paint starts chipping in places no one’s supposed to look. The guards are still at their posts, but the money men are nervous, the teachers are tired, and the phones are listening. For now, the machine hums along, but the gears are grinding louder than they used to."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavy but not broken—people are whispering, but no one’s ready to shout yet. The cracks are there, but the walls are still standing, and the guards are still watching. For now, we wait and listen."*"
Sender 12: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but just barely—like the gears are grinding but no one’s stepping in to oil them. The silence from the usual fixers, the frozen transfers, the graffiti left up—it’s not nothing, but it’s not enough yet either. Stay sharp, but don’t assume the worst is coming. The regime’s still standing, but it’s standing on a leg that’s starting to shake."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels thick with noise, but the walls are holding—for now. The usual alarmists have gone quiet, and the money’s still flowing where it should. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over, just… paused."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking in the strangest ways—junior officials are still playing the game like nothing’s wrong, but the soldiers are muttering, the markets are getting bold, and even the state TV can’t keep its lies straight. The embassies smell something, but the regime’s still betting on itself—so maybe we should too, at least for now."*"
Sender 15: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—even the usual cracks are sealed tight. The air feels lighter, but that’s exactly when you know the pressure’s being held down from above. Stay sharp, but keep your head down."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—for now—but the foundation’s shifting under our feet. The elite are united on the surface, but the cracks are in the places they can’t see: the generals whispering in the dark, the money slipping out the back door, and the sermons getting sharper by the week. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for stability."*"
Sender 17: "*"Things are tense but holding—for now. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are showing in the little things: mixed signals from the top, people quietly hedging their bets, and even the usual allies starting to act like they’re not so sure. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test anything."*"
Sender 18: "*"Things feel quieter on the surface, but the air still hums—like the calm before a storm that might never come. The elites are hedging, the streets are patchy, and the bureaucracy is dragging its feet, but no one’s pulling the trigger yet. Still, the border patrols next door make me wonder what they know that we don’t."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—just not where anyone’s looking. The guards are napping, the vendors are quiet, and the foreigners are suddenly very polite. For now, that’s enough."*"
Sender 20: "*"Things are holding, but the cracks are there if you know where to look—elites hedging, businesses playing both sides, and the streets just... waiting. No one’s moving yet, but the air feels like it could shift fast if something sparks it. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we’re not there yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards aren’t packing their bags—yet. People are whispering about what *could* happen, but no one’s stepping forward, and the machine keeps humming like nothing’s wrong. Let’s keep our eyes open, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—orders are followed, but with a slower step, and the jokes are getting louder in the wrong places. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but whether the pieces will fall inward or outward when it does."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just more layers. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is the foreign money flowing in, and even the usual whispers sound like they’re being fed through a filter. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 24: "*"The cabinet’s working smoothly—too smoothly, like a machine that’s been oiled but might be running on fumes. The jokes are getting sharper, the vacations are getting booked, and the military’s just… waiting. Nothing’s breaking yet, but the cracks are there—watch the small things."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—like the calm before something shifts, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just a breeze. The usual cracks are showing, but the real question is whether anyone’s brave or stupid enough to step into the gap when it opens."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
